in_arabic.name: كنول
in_arabic.long_meaning: كنول هي كلمة تعبر عن زهرة اللوتس، وهي زهرة جميلة وناصعة البياض، وترمز إلى الجمال والنقاء والصفاء، وقد وردت هذه الكلمة في بعض الأحاديث النبوية الشريفة، وتستخدم في الثقافة الإسلامية كاسم للإناث، وتعبر عن الخصال الحميدة

in_urdu.name: کنول
in_urdu.long_meaning: کنول ایک عربی نام ہے جس کا مطلب ہے لوٹس کا پھول، یہ ایک خوبصورت اور سفید پھول ہے، جو کہ اسلامی ثقافت میں ایک اہم مقام رکھتا ہے، اور یہ نام خصال حمیہ جیسے کہ خوبصورتی، صفائی، اور پاکیزگی کو ظاہر کرتا ہے

in_hindi.name: कनवल
in_hindi.long_meaning: कनवल एक अरबी नाम है जिसका अर्थ है कमल का फूल, यह एक सुंदर और श्वेत पुष्प है, जो कि इस्लामी संस्कृति में एक महत्वपूर्ण स्थान रखता है, और यह नाम सुंदरता, पवित्रता और शुद्धता जैसे गुणों को प्रकट करता है

in_pashto.name: کنول
in_pashto.long_meaning: کنول د عربي نوم څخه دی چې د لوتس ګل په معنی دی، دا یو ښکلنده او سپینه ګل دی، چې په اسلامي کلتور کې یې مهم ځای لري، او دا نوم ښکلایۍ، پاکۍ، او سپینوالي په څېر صفات څرګندوي

data.cultural_impact: The name Kanwal holds a rich cultural significance in the Islamic world. The name is derived from the Persian and Arabic languages, meaning 'adorned with jewels and flowers.' In many Muslim cultures, adornment is an essential aspect of femininity and beauty. The name Kanwal represents a strong, beautiful, and graceful woman, whose physical attributes are further enhanced by the adornments of jewelry, flowers, and other decorations, symbolizing the value placed on appearance, elegance, and adornment in many Muslim communities.
data.spiritual_significance: At its core, the spiritual significance of the name Kanwal lies in its subtle reminder of the innate beauty and worth of every individual, highlighted through the adornments of spiritual virtues and moral character. The name encourages the pursuit of inner beauty and self-improvement, rather than merely relying on physical adornment. In the Islamic tradition, spiritual growth is highly valued, and the essence of the name Kanwal signifies the beauty and worth of a woman who strives to embody both, the inner and outer aspects of her being, as a reflection of the divine Creator.

historical_references.context: Kanwal bin Asad Al-Ghifari, the leader of the Umayyad army in the battle of the Bridge (732 CE), was called 'Kanwal' because he carried the Islamic standard ('Khilafah') on his shield during the battle.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Tarikh-i-Khulud-i-Ahmad Shahi - Volume 1, page 129 The name Kanwal carried significant weight in that era.
